{{Infobox NCAA Athlete | name = Jon Brockman | image = | caption = | college = [[University of Washington|Washington]] | conference = [[Pac-10 Conference|Pac-10]] | sport = [[Basketball]] | position = Power Forward | jersey = 40 | class = Senior | career_start = 2006 | career_end = 2009 | nickname = | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 7 | weight_lb = 255 | nationality = [[United States|American]] | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1987|3|20}} | birth_place = [[Snohomish, Washington]] | highschool = Snohomish High School }} '''Jon Brockman''' (born March 20, 1987 in [[Snohomish, Washington]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player; the starting power forward and team captain for the [[University of Washington]] men's basketball team. He grabbed the 1,000th rebound of his career on December 30, 2008 in a win over Morgan State,[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283650264 Morgan State 67, Washington 81 - Recap - December 30, 2008] and became Washington's all-time leading rebounder on January 15, 2009 in a win over [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], breaking Doug Smart's school record of 1,051.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290152483 Washington 84, Oregon 67 - Recap - January 15, 2009] == College career == === Sophomore Year === Games: 32
Games Started: 31
Team Record: 20-12
Field Goal Pct: 55%
Point Avg: 14.2
Rebound Avg: 9.6
F-Throw Pct: 66%
Steals: 24
Avg Minutes: 28.8 Won 5 team awards including MVP at the annual Washington men's basketball banquet. 15 double-doubles led the Pac-10 Conference. Ranked 3rd among Pac-10 in field goal percentage (55.0%). Leader of Conference with 9.6 rebounds per game. One of nine player to receive Pac-10's Complete Conference Honors. === Freshman Year === Games: 33
Games Started: 32
Team Record: 26-7
Field Goal Pct: 51.8%
Point Avg: 8.4
Rebound Avg: 6.5
F-Throw Pct: 66.7%
Steals: 35
Avg Minutes: 22.1 Played with future NBA players [[Brandon Roy]] and [[Bobby Jones (basketball, born 1984)|Bobby Jones]]. Was named to the PAC-10 all Freshman team. Played in the NCAA Tournament, lost to UConn in the Sweet 16. Led Huskies in rebounds and was 7th in the Pac-10. Ended the season with 4 double-doubles. Second highest total rebounds by a freshman in Husky history. Was ranked 2nd in the Pac-10 with his 51.8 field goal percentage. == High School Career == '''Senior Year'''
Point Avg.: 30.2
Rebound Avg: 14 '''Junior Year'''
Point Avg.: 22.4
Rebound Avg: 13 Brockman attended Snohomish High School and was a 4-year letterman and played alongside his brother for two years. Ranked as the 20th prospect in the country and 5th among power forwards by Scout.com. Named to the McDonalds All-America Team in 2005. Made the semifinals in the 2005 High School Slam Dunk Competition. Third leading scorer in the state of Washington in the 2004-05 season.
